candidates.evidence_text: From Alan Bennett to Sir Alex Ferguson, Betty Boothroyd to Bez and Fred Dibnah to Iain Duncan Smith, Paul Wolfgang Webster has photographed a wide range of well-known faces across his decades-long career, but one eluded him As a punk, he always wanted to capture an icon of the scene, Dame Vivienne Westwood, but never had the opportunity That was until the fashion legend turned up at an anti-fracking protest in Lancashire in 2018 Discussing the event ahead of an exhibition of his unseen photographs from that day, Wolfgang said the encounter was everything he had always hoped it would be, adding: "It was like she was Joan of Arc, walking down the street with this big crusade of people behind her." candidates.summary: Connie Kerr used to dread being asked if she was a mum. Now she is breaking the stigma with her truth

candidates.lead: Connie Kerr used to dread being asked if she was a mum.
candidates.evidence_text: For years, that was the question Connie Kerr dreaded Connie, from Manchester, said she had done "all the right things". She had a successful career, a husband and assumed children would follow But after four miscarriages in the space of two years, the future she imagined for herself was taken away She said she was reminded daily of what she had lost. From television adverts to workplace small talk, Connie felt everything reinforced the message that a woman without children was somehow incomplete More than a decade later, she has turned her experiences into a play and hopes to challenge the taboos that still surround childlessness, miscarriage and infertility Connie spoke to BBC News ahead of Baby Loss Awareness Week about why she wants to encourage conversations about a subject she believes is still taboo

candidates.lead: Shakespeare's famous play will be performed at the nightclub in an effort to engage "new audiences"
candidates.evidence_text: While the Oldham Coliseum Theatre's doors remain closed during its major revamp, the creative team has needed to think outside the box when deciding where to temporarily decamp They have chosen the last remaining nightclub in the Greater Manchester town to stage William Shakespeare's Macbeth "I want to blow the dust off Shakespeare," said the Coliseum's new creative director Nick Bagnall "This isn't about putting the play on a pedestal, it's about creating an experience that grabs people by the throat, whether they have seen Macbeth 10 times or never encountered it before "We want people who have never set foot in a theatre to walk into Liquid and Envy and feel this story belongs to them "Staging Macbeth inside a working Oldham nightclub creates its own intrigue."

candidates.evidence_text: Celebrations begin in Oldham for nine-day Hindu festival Navratri - BBC News Image source, BHARAT KUMAR SISODIA Image caption, The nine-day festival of dancing begins on Sunday By Rebecca Brahde North West Published 11 October 2026 Celebrations for a nine-day Hindu festival of dancing are set to get underway across Manchester. Navratri, which runs until 20 October, celebrates Durga, the mother goddess who carries weapons in her arms, and marks her nine-day battle with evil demon Mahishasura. One of the most important celebrations in the Hindu calendar, communities across the North West will celebrate with dancing, gift-giving, light, and food, including in Oldham which is hosting free events throughout the period. Bharat Kumar Sisodia from the Indian Association in Oldham said it was the "major festival of the year." Image source, BHARATKUMARSISODIA Image caption, Free celebrations are being hosted by the Indian Association in Oldham Goddess Durga, "became nine different forms, and each day represents her different powers," he said. The festival ends with what's known as Dussehra, which is the celebration of good over evil, as Durga defeats Mahishasura, meaning that "peace across the world was restored," he said. "In all festivals we have lights, sweets, gifts, prayers and singing, but this particular festival is nine days of dancing." Image source, BHARAT KUMAR SISODIA Image caption, Hundreds attend the events in Oldham The form of dancing, includes Garba, which sees participants move in circles around an idol of the goddess Durga, as well as Raas Dandiya, in which dancers use a pair of decorated wooden sticks, striking them with a partner. He said that during the dancing, "you feel that you are all connected with the divinity, and everyone else." "It is a nice social gathering, where the community just gets together," he continued. The Indian Association in Oldham is holding daily free celebrations between 19:00 and 23:00 BST until Tuesday at Shree Radha Krishna Mandir in Schofield Street. candidates.lead: Barbara Gould has left an 'incredible legacy' in Middleton, Rochdale after 37 years service
candidates.evidence_text: Lollipop lady who is 'credit to Middleton' retires after 37 years - BBC News Image source, ROCHDALE BOROUGH COUNCIL Image caption, Mum Jodie, her son Nathaniel and Barbara who is retiring after 37 years By Rebecca Brahde North West Published 11 October 2026 A much-loved lollipop lady who has been a "credit to the Middleton area" has retired after 37 years. Barbara Gould started her career at St Thomas More Primary and St Michael's Primary School in Rochdale, where she was also a lunchtime supervisor. She later moved to the crossing at Grimshaw Lane, where she supported children from schools including Alkrington Primary School and St Peter's Primary School. She said: "I've enjoyed my job tremendously. It's the joy of getting up and knowing who I will be seeing." "The children always have a smile and they speak to me and share their problems. She said she has even "had the pleasure" of helping the children of former pupils she had also helped. 'Incredible legacy' Gould said despite the fact she would "really miss the children" she is looking forward to spending more time with her family. Mum Jodie Ward said her son Nathaniel has loved seeing Barbara every day on his walk to school. She said: "Nathaniel is autistic and he sometimes struggles to talk to people, but he loves seeing Barbara every day and he always tells her what he's been doing. "He will really miss her." Councillor Dylan Williams from Rochdale Borough Council, who was helped by Barbara to cross roads as a pupil more than 20 years ago, said he "remembered her from all those years ago." He added: "Everybody knows Barbara. She has a lovely presence. "I know that she will have stopped countless children getting hurt on our roads over the years and that's an incredible legacy she can walk away with. "She's been a credit to council and to the Middleton area and absolutely deserves a wonderful retirement," he added. candidates.evidence_text: Warning to drivers as part of Bury M60 to shut again - BBC News Image caption, Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday evening By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 9 October 2026 Updated 10 October 2026 Drivers are being warned of "severe congestion" when a busy stretch of motorway is closed this weekend as part of an upgrade to the road. Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday night until 06:00 on Monday. The closures are to enable the demolition of two large overhead gantries at the Simister Island Interchange. It comes after two others were removed last month. National Highways said the work was part of a £300m improvement scheme and would improve traffic flow, support future housing, employment and growth across the region. Frances Oliver, of National Highways, told BBC North West Tonight : "These gantries are up to 120 tonnes so it's very similar to removing a small footbridge so it is quite a large amount of work for us to undertake." Image caption, Two busy junctions at Simister and Prestwich will be closed for the work Oliver added: "We are expecting there to be severe congestion in the area so we are asking people to plan their journeys, check before they travel and if at all try not to travel or defer their journey. "The message is if you don't need to be in the area please try not to be." candidates.evidence_text: Three young politicians from across the north-west of England have called on the government to rethink plans to axe the UK Youth Parliament (UKYP) The parliament - which has more than 300 elected members aged between 11 and 18 - was established in 1999 to boost interest in politics among young people The Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) is not committed to funding the parliament beyond March 2027, leading to speculation it could close "Without UKYP, we are losing a role that young people trust, aspire to be and understand they have their support," warned Poppy Williams "As the elected member for Knowsley, I have had young people reach out to me for support and advice." The 16-year-old said she had wanted to become a member of the UKYP to "show young people that no matter what accent they carry, the clothes that they wear and the household that they come from, their voices matter"

The scheme would see 192 homes built on empty land next to the old Lock Keepers site All the homes will be available for affordable rates (up to 80 per cent of market value), say developers CERT and True North Partnerships. The plans include three apartment buildings and a series of duplex homes at ground level, ‘arranged to maximise natural light and views acros When the vision was first revealed earlier this year, locals were shocked by the scale of the plans, given the site is only 0.93 hectare The developers say they have carried out a consultation and used the feedback to shape elements of the scheme. But nearby residents claim they are struggling to see what changes have actually been made Celia Poole lives in Bridgewater House, just next to the proposed project. She said the scheme was triple the expected size

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Letting agent attacked by XL Bully called Tank after owner told it to 'get him' John Walkden, 62, was handed a suspended jail term Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:00, 12 Oct 2026 Updated 06:07, 12 Oct 2026 View 2 Imag A letting agent was set upon by an XL Bully after its owner told it to 'get him'. John Walkden , 62, had been living at a rented property in Bolton but had been having issues with cleanliness As a result James Melly, the letting agent, had spoken to him on multiple occasions. During one visit, Walkden became aggressive towards Mr Melly before ordering his dog, Tank, to attack him After around five minutes of goading Tank to 'get him', the dog jumped up at Mr Melly and scratched his arm Walkden pleaded guilty to being an owner in change of a dog dangerously out of control causing injury, and was handed a suspended jail term. He was also banned from owning dogs for five years and Tank was ordered to be destroyed At Manchester Crown Court , Olivia Brooksbank-Laing, prosecuting, said that Mr Melly has repeatedly spoken to Walkden about issues with cleanliness in the property, and the local authority had become involved

He had no ID, wallet, keys, phone or watch So began began the search to identify the mystery man of Dovestones . He was lying on the patch of grass off the steep Chew Track, about 400m above Chew reservoir

The scheme would see 192 homes built on empty land next to the old Lock Keepers site All the homes will be available for affordable rates (up to 80 per cent of market value), say developers CERT and True North Partnerships. The plans include three apartment buildings and a series of duplex homes at ground level, ‘arranged to maximise natural light and views acros When the vision was first revealed earlier this year, locals were shocked by the scale of the plans, given the site is only 0.93 hectare The developers say they have carried out a consultation and used the feedback to shape elements of the scheme. But nearby residents claim they are struggling to see what changes have actually been made Celia Poole lives in Bridgewater House, just next to the proposed project. candidates.evidence_text: Chorlton Man arrested after 'windows explode' as emergency services descend on Chorlton flat fire It's understood the man remained in police custody on Monday morning Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 07:26, 12 Oct 2026 View 2 Images A man was arrested after a fire broke out inside a flat above a shop in Chorlton . Greater Manchester Police confirmed he was held on suspicion of arson No age for him has been released. It's understood the man remained in police custody on Monday morning A police cordon was put in place on Sunday night after the incident on Barlow Moor Road. Photos and videos from the scene show leaping flames coming from the second floor window above BBM Bargains on the busy road, one of a row of businesses The fire is believed to have started at around 8.30pm. There were multiple fire engines and police cars at the scene as officers trained their hoses on the building A road closure was in place from the end of the row of shops up to the junction with Hardy Lane and Mauldeth Road West

candidates.evidence_text: Heaton Park Fury as oil spill on Heaton Park boating lake kills bird with others badly injured One bird sadly had to be put to sleep Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 06:44, 12 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Coots, swans and The waterfowl on Heaton Park boating lake had to be rescued from the water and taken to a centre for urgent treatment after a reported oil spill on the lake coated their feathers Kirklees Valley Wildlife Rescue shared the news on Facebook on Sunday (October 11) confirming that they had been at the park on Wednesday and Thursday (October 7 and 8) this week to rescue the animals The Heaton Park and Hall Facebook account confirmed that the charity had 'temporarily rehomed' the birds due to a report of a contaminant in the water "Our Estates team are taking advice from the Environment Agency to address this issue," they said. In an update on Sunday (October 11), the rescue centre shared photos of the birds being rescued, with the tragic update that one had to be put to sleep

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Letting agent attacked by XL Bully called Tank after owner told it to 'get him' John Walkden, 62, was handed a suspended jail term Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:00, 12 Oct 2026 Updated 06:07, 12 Oct 2026 View 2 Imag A letting agent was set upon by an XL Bully after its owner told it to 'get him'. John Walkden , 62, had been living at a rented property in Bolton but had been having issues with cleanliness As a result James Melly, the letting agent, had spoken to him on multiple occasions. During one visit, Walkden became aggressive towards Mr Melly before ordering his dog, Tank, to attack him After around five minutes of goading Tank to 'get him', the dog jumped up at Mr Melly and scratched his arm Walkden pleaded guilty to being an owner in change of a dog dangerously out of control causing injury, and was handed a suspended jail term. He was also banned from owning dogs for five years and Tank was ordered to be destroyed At Manchester Crown Court , Olivia Brooksbank-Laing, prosecuting, said that Mr Melly has repeatedly spoken to Walkden about issues with cleanliness in the property, and the local authority had become involved

Music played throughout the streets of Moss Side and Hulme . Bright costumes, flags and feathers moved through the crowds as the parade made its way through Alexandra Park, continuing a tradition that dates back to 1971. For most people, the festival was about music, culture and But amid the noise and colour was a less conspicuous presence. Stuck to a lamppost near the (visible) police presence was a sign warning visitors that live facial recognition (LFR) was being used in the area Every carnival goer walking through the entrance had their faces scanned and checked against a police watchlist “We take your privacy very seriously,” the sign read, somewhat ironically View 8 Images Police used facial recognition technology at the Manchester Carnival (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: True crime series The mystery man of Dovestones In 2015 an elderly man was found dead on a remote track above Dovestones reservoir. It was the start of a 13 month mystery that sparked worldwide interest and a global investigation View 6 Images The dis Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:00, 12 Oct 2026 The man was found lying on his back. He was fully-clothed His arms were at sides and his feet were facing downhill. In his right trouser pocket was £130 in £10 notes. In his left coat pocket were three train tickets and an empty medicine container But what he wasn't carrying was just as important. He had no ID, wallet, keys, phone or watch So began began the search to identify the mystery man of Dovestones . It was an investigation that sparked worldwide interest and took detectives from a rocky outcrop on Saddleworth Moor, to the leafy suburbs of West London and the city of Lahore in Pakistan The body of Neil Dovestones , as he would be nicknamed by mortuary workers at Royal Oldham Hospital, was found by cyclist Stuart Crowther at around 10.50am on Saturday, December 12, 2015. He was lying on the patch of grass off the steep Chew Track, about 400m above Chew reservoir

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Carrington Relief Road: Hundreds of objections, £132 million, and just 15-years until it hits capacity The Carrington Relief Road is a very expensive, hugely controversial plan that campaigners say will cause 'severe and permanent harm', but Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 19:30, 11 Oct 2026 The controversial Carrington Relief Road comes with a whopping £132m price tag, but parts will be operating near capacity within just 15 years, documents show The relief road has been touted by political leaders as the solution to traffic woes in the area around Partington and Carrington . The project aims to divert traffic away from the A6144, reducing congestion and improving travel times for drivers and public transport users But traffic modelling data published by Trafford council reveals that by 2045 two sections of the route, including a key junction, will hit more than 90pc capacity – the point at which severe congestion is thought to be highly probable. The road is not expected to open until afte The 2.7-mile road would link the A6144 Manchester Road to the west with the A6144 Carrington Spur in the east. It forms a key part of the council’s New Carrington plan which will ultimately see around 5,000 new homes and 350,000sqm of new employment space built View 4 Images Artist's impression of the proposed Carrington Relief Road (Image: One Trafford Partnership)

Wain Estates, who own the land, are currently preparing a planning application to But a new viability report created by surveyor Mark Anthony Smith on behalf of the council has found ‘reopening Swinton Park for golf use is financially viable’ and there is local demand for the sport Campaigners believe the document could be ‘vital’ in successfully opposing a planning application David Marsh, one of the figureheads of the Save Swinton Golf Club campaign, explained: “The land use was originally agreed as for golf. So developers will try and get around that by claiming there’s no need for golf here anymore. But it’s clear there definitely is. This could giv “It’s a really important place. candidates.evidence_text: Moss Side Man detained in Turkey and arrested for murder after pair shot dead in Manchester Cheriff Tall and Abayomi 'Junior' Ajose were both gunned down in Moss Side in 2020 Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:15, 11 Oct 2 A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after two men were shot dead in Moss Side in 2020. Cheriff Tall, 21, and Abayomi 'Junior' Ajose, 36, were both gunned down in a car park in June that year. It followed an argument at a lockdown party The double fatal shooting happened shortly before 1am on June 21, 2020, at a party in a car park off Caythorpe Street in Moss Side. A gunman shot Mr Tall first, and 20 seconds later blasted 'Good Samaritan' Mr Ajose who had stepped in to help Today, in a major update, police have revealed a 36-year-old man was detained in Turkey before being flown to Stansted Airport in London yesterday (October 10) where he was met by Greater Manchester Police officers Police have previously offered a £50,000 reward for key information that leads to the discovery and conviction of the pair’s killer. About 400 people had attended the party but Greater Manchester Police said the force has faced 'reluctance' from those at the scene to come forward At an inquest in 2024, Manchester Area Coroner Zak Golombek, recording unlawful killing verdicts, appealed for witnesses to come forward to help bring justice to the families and said: "These were senseless acts of violence against two innocent individuals."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Moss Side Man detained in Turkey and arrested for murder after pair shot dead in Manchester Cheriff Tall and Abayomi 'Junior' Ajose were both gunned down in Moss Side in 2020 Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:15, 11 Oct 2 A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after two men were shot dead in Moss Side in 2020. Cheriff Tall, 21, and Abayomi 'Junior' Ajose, 36, were both gunned down in a car park in June that year. It followed an argument at a lockdown party The double fatal shooting happened shortly before 1am on June 21, 2020, at a party in a car park off Caythorpe Street in Moss Side. A gunman shot Mr Tall first, and 20 seconds later blasted 'Good Samaritan' Mr Ajose who had stepped in to help Today, in a major update, police have revealed a 36-year-old man was detained in Turkey before being flown to Stansted Airport in London yesterday (October 10) where he was met by Greater Manchester Police officers Police have previously offered a £50,000 reward for key information that leads to the discovery and conviction of the pair’s killer. About 400 people had attended the party but Greater Manchester Police said the force has faced 'reluctance' from those at the scene to come forward At an inquest in 2024, Manchester Area Coroner Zak Golombek, recording unlawful killing verdicts, appealed for witnesses to come forward to help bring justice to the families and said: "These were senseless acts of violence against two innocent individuals."

candidates.evidence_text: Football Fans clash with police outside Anfield after Man City defeat Liverpool Police deployed pepper spray to keep Liverpool fans back Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 19:57, 11 Oc There were scuffles between fans and police outside Anfield Stadium this evening (October 11) after Manchester City defeated Liverpool in their first match since they were found guilty of breaching financial regulations Today's clash with one of their biggest rivals Liverpool was billed by many as a tricky first fixture back for City after the Nations' League international break, with a hostile Anfield atmosphere expected to make life difficult for them after the news broke of their guilty verdi But despite banners taunting fans of 'cheat's and 'tainted glory', after a goalless first half, City ultimately quietened the home fans with a 3-0 victory after Liverpool went down to ten men The away fans and players managed to largely avoid the Liverpool crowds as they entered the stadium, but M.E.N reporter Chris Slater reported some 'handbags' between home fans and police outside the away end after the match came to an end As City fans made their way away from the ground inside a barrier of police officers, Liverpool fans on the other side traded angry words and gestures with the departing fans

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Letting agent attacked by XL Bully called Tank after owner told it to 'get him' John Walkden, 62, was handed a suspended jail term Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:00, 12 Oct 2026 Updated 06:07, 12 Oct 2026 View 2 Imag A letting agent was set upon by an XL Bully after its owner told it to 'get him'. John Walkden , 62, had been living at a rented property in Bolton but had been having issues with cleanliness As a result James Melly, the letting agent, had spoken to him on multiple occasions. During one visit, Walkden became aggressive towards Mr Melly before ordering his dog, Tank, to attack him After around five minutes of goading Tank to 'get him', the dog jumped up at Mr Melly and scratched his arm Walkden pleaded guilty to being an owner in change of a dog dangerously out of control causing injury, and was handed a suspended jail term. He was also banned from owning dogs for five years and Tank was ordered to be destroyed At Manchester Crown Court , Olivia Brooksbank-Laing, prosecuting, said that Mr Melly has repeatedly spoken to Walkden about issues with cleanliness in the property, and the local authority had become involved

Music played throughout the streets of Moss Side and Hulme . Bright costumes, flags and feathers moved through the crowds as the parade made its way through Alexandra Park, continuing a tradition that dates back to 1971. For most people, the festival was about music, culture and But amid the noise and colour was a less conspicuous presence. Stuck to a lamppost near the (visible) police presence was a sign warning visitors that live facial recognition (LFR) was being used in the area Every carnival goer walking through the entrance had their faces scanned and checked against a police watchlist “We take your privacy very seriously,” the sign read, somewhat ironically View 8 Images Police used facial recognition technology at the Manchester Carnival (Image: Manchester Evening News)

The project aims to divert traffic away from the A6144, reducing congestion and improving travel times for drivers and public transport users But traffic modelling data published by Trafford council reveals that by 2045 two sections of the route, including a key junction, will hit more than 90pc capacity – the point at which severe congestion is thought to be highly probable. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Unmissable An 180-year old church has disappeared overnight, and people are angry As yellow diggers crush the 186-year-old Grade II listed All Souls Church on Every Street, heritage campaigners and heartbroken Ancoats residents demand answers over how Add to preferred sources News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:02, 11 Oct 2026 The videos are not an easy watch The maw of a digger delicately, painstakingly, begins to work at the wall, sinking its metal teeth down into the brickwork, shedding dust like a snow shower as it finally bites down on the window, the delicate stained glass folding like a piece of film reel before falling lamely A yellow digger arm reaches its long sinew up and slowly, almost apologetically, topples one of the pointed, gothic, Grade II listed towers which has loomed over this area of Ancoats for almost two centuries And what is left at the end? Cheriff Tall, 21, and Abayomi 'Junior' Ajose, 36, were both gunned down in a car park in June that year. It followed an argument at a lockdown party The double fatal shooting happened shortly before 1am on June 21, 2020, at a party in a car park off Caythorpe Street in Moss Side. A gunman shot Mr Tall first, and 20 seconds later blasted 'Good Samaritan' Mr Ajose who had stepped in to help Today, in a major update, police have revealed a 36-year-old man was detained in Turkey before being flown to Stansted Airport in London yesterday (October 10) where he was met by Greater Manchester Police officers Police have previously offered a £50,000 reward for key information that leads to the discovery and conviction of the pair’s killer. About 400 people had attended the party but Greater Manchester Police said the force has faced 'reluctance' from those at the scene to come forward At an inquest in 2024, Manchester Area Coroner Zak Golombek, recording unlawful killing verdicts, appealed for witnesses to come forward to help bring justice to the families and said: "These were senseless acts of violence against two innocent individuals."

Begging at some of the region's busiest junction But it seems to have become more common in recent months, across more of the region's roads. Those involved are often putting themselves at risk People are regularly seen walking past queues of traffic asking for money, or sitting at traffic islands between hectic crossroads. It's a heartbreaking sight that comes at a time when the government is pushing to eradicate rough sleeping It's understood that police who work supporting vulnerable people in Greater Manchester believe the increase is partly down to the repeal of the historic Vagrancy Act - which dated back to 1824 - in June this year. That move officially decriminalised begging and rough sleeping in But there is also an understanding that begging on major roads, while drivers often face long queues of traffic, is believed to be more lucrative than in other places. Effectively, people in tough situations are willing to take the risk to their personal safety

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale How a deal to sell the historic Hopwood Hall for £1 led to a bitter High Court battle Ever since Rochdale council cut ties with Hopwood DePree over teh Grade-II* listed building in October 2024, a war has raged View 6 Images Hopwood DePree Add to preferred sources News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:13, 10 Oct 2026 When an American filmmaker and Rochdale council signed an agreement over a shared ambition to restore Hopwood Hall, no one could have fathomed the furious saga that unfolded What started as a harmonious relationship between Hopwood DePree and the local authority ended up with them being on opposite sides of a court room Mr DePree claims ancestral connections to the Grade-II* listed building in Middleton . His dream was to bring the 1400s stately home back to life. He even roped in the local community to help him do it, apparently spending more than £750,000 on the project On what he described as a ‘sad day’ in Manchester Civil Justice Centre last week, his dream was crushed. The High Court ruled in favour of the council following a legal battle over whether Mr DePree had the right to buy the estate or not The saga began in 2017 when Hopwood DePree signed an options agreement with town hall bosses to lead the redevelopment of the hall. Since then he has led a decade-long community effort to do exactly that

candidates.evidence_text: Tuesday 6 October 2026 at 5:15pm Zac Bolland and and his accomplice David Worrall were both given four life sentences for the petrol bombing. Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

Under the arrangements, Chief Executive Shelley Kipling will co The four Interim Lead Member portfolios have been allocated to the Council's four largest political groups, with deputy roles assigned from the same groups The Resources portfolio will provide political oversight of the Council's finances, budget management, transformation programme, corporate services, governance, workforce and organisational performance

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Libraries across the borough are teaming up with a local charity to help families access thousands of free pre-loved school uniforms and shoes As families continue to manage the high costs of school uniform, households cannot always afford the necessary items needed for their child This has led to growing demand for affordable alternatives, including a reliance on local charities like Uniform For All, which Rochdale Borough Council is working with to support those who need extra help Every day high-quality pre-loved items, including polo shirts, skirts, trousers, branded school blazers, coats and pumps, are given to families through the charity However, not every family has the resources to travel long distances to collect their orders That is why Rochdale’s library service is helping to collect these items so families can pick them up closer to where they live at their nearest library and save on additional travel costs

candidates.evidence_text: The need for invasive post-mortems across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham could be reduced by up to 80 per cent thanks to pioneering new digital autopsies The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Borough Council, said

candidates.evidence_text: A former pub transformed into sheltered accommodation for those struggling with homelessness has been described as a 'blueprint' to be replicated across the country Earlier this year, the former Queens Arms in Newtown was unveiled as a refurbished 14-bed sheltered accommodation, complete with kitchen and washing facilities, to give people in crisis a safe place to stay and receive further support to get back on their feet With homelessness in the national spotlight following Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s pledge to end rough sleeping, it is venues like the Queens Arms and the work of organisations like The Brick and Wigan Council that are being assessed to achieve these aims Councillor Susan Gambles, portfolio holder for housing and welfare, and chair of the homelessness and rough sleeping strategic partnership board, said: “There are some fantastic local partners that work collectively to support people at risk of homelessness, and we are so pleased “What comes across very strongly at their Queens Arms hub is that people are thriving there; they are positive, moving forward, and believing in themselves, and I think that is down to the facilities, the camaraderie, and the staff who care very deeply “This is the template that we should be using across the country, so we will continue championing these services and requesting more funding to be able to do even more like this.”

candidates.evidence_text: A rogue trader who targeted vulnerable residents and carried out unnecessary and substandard roofing work has been sentenced to more than five years in prison following a prosecution brought by Wigan Council's Trading Standards team At a hearing at Bolton Crown Court on Wednesday 2th September, Tyrone Young, the owner of ACL Roofing and Staydry, was sentenced in his absence to a total of 5 years and 4 months in prison after pleading guilty to fraud and trading regulatory offences, with a warrant outstanding At the sentencing hearing, it was explained that Young had previously received a suspended sentence at Burnley Crown Court in December 2022, for offences in which he “coerced people and did unnecessary and inadequate work” Despite this, Young breached the terms of his sentence and was sent to prison. Yet within a month of his release, he committed similar offences in Wigan Borough in September 2023. This involved the business owner “lying about his name, advising work was required when it wasn’t, i In February 2024, the court heard that Young committed offences against a second victim, where he “cold called the victim, lied to them, made false assertions, and was deliberately aggressive and intimidating”, with the completed work also described as “unnecessary and inadequate With the help of Trading Standards officers, the victims read out powerful personal impact statements to the court, explaining how Young’s coercive and unscrupulous behaviour had devastated them. One victim was living with a terminally ill husband and now can’t afford to fix her

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

candidates.evidence_text: History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. Venue The Warehouse, Aviva Studios, Water Street, Manchester, M3 4JQ . . History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

The interior showcases the works The famous cocktail menu will return, featuring favourites like the Pink Picante, Pomme Verte – a popular twist on an appletini, Belfast Coffee, the famous spicy pickle martini Especiado and the Pornstar Chic, crafted with homemade passionfruit sorbet Red Light also introduces a brand-new savoury snack menu, including, Boquerones, Pickled Guindilla peppers, Gordal olives, Mini Croissant Butter Blondies from Pollen and homemade Salted Popcorn Ice Cream. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. candidates.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
candidates.reason: LLM-review: Новые данные: падение акций Nvidia на 3,4%, SoftBank на 10,7% после слов Амодеи | Validator: previous publication found on 2026-10-11; plan-digest will make the final repeat decision (provisional=exact_fingerprint_unchanged_evidence, anchor=local_action, ttl=1d). | Selection: Selected in tech_business shortlist before writing.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть обновление, которое может быть полезно в сегодняшней сводке.
candidates.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

Fro Alongside browsing and buying, visitors can enjoy an inspiring programme of talks, live demonstrations and hands-on workshops featuring exciting names from the worlds of craft, design and food. Highlights include free drop-in animation workshops using clay, food and other materia “GNCCF offers a connection you simply can’t get online or on the high street – the chance to meet the makers, hear the stories behind the work and invest in beautifully made pieces that will be cherished for years to come.”

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Football Fans clash with police outside Anfield after Man City defeat Liverpool Police deployed pepper spray to keep Liverpool fans back Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 19:57, 11 Oc There were scuffles between fans and police outside Anfield Stadium this evening (October 11) after Manchester City defeated Liverpool in their first match since they were found guilty of breaching financial regulations Today's clash with one of their biggest rivals Liverpool was billed by many as a tricky first fixture back for City after the Nations' League international break, with a hostile Anfield atmosphere expected to make life difficult for them after the news broke of their guilty verdi But despite banners taunting fans of 'cheat's and 'tainted glory', after a goalless first half, City ultimately quietened the home fans with a 3-0 victory after Liverpool went down to ten men The away fans and players managed to largely avoid the Liverpool crowds as they entered the stadium, but M.E.N reporter Chris Slater reported some 'handbags' between home fans and police outside the away end after the match came to an end As City fans made their way away from the ground inside a barrier of police officers, Liverpool fans on the other side traded angry words and gestures with the departing fans

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Elliot Anderson makes Liverpool atmosphere admission after Man City's 115 charges verdict Manchester City's players entered a hostile atmosphere at Anfield but overcame it to beat Liverpool 3-0 and continue their 100 per cent record this season A Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson admitted that the atmosphere was 'more than normal' at Anfield, after beating Liverpool 3-0 in the Premier League . This was City's first game since an independent panel found them guilty of almost all of the Premier League charges level Due to the manner of the verdict, and the rivalry between Liverpool and City , a hostile environment was expected at Anfield. Concerns about the team bus potentially being attacked were raised pre-match but, after using an alternative entrance, the City team arrived at the ground However, once the game kicked off, the City players were greeted with boos, jeers and chants of 'cheats' and 'going down', from an angry home support. When asked about the atmosphere after the game, Anderson told Sky Sports: "It was more than normal, arriving into Anfield and the Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! "We did well to quieten the crowd. [We] struggled first half but second we were better and then the goals came. I think I just enjoy it, I enjoy the crowd and I enjoy the noise, I thrive under it and that is when I really come alive and it gives me confidence."

Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти.
